cues: DNA is the genetic material, as Griffith, Avery and Hershey and Chase showed, though some viruses use RNA.
It is an antiparallel double helix, A with T by two bonds, G with C by three, two nanometres wide, three point four per turn.
It replicates semi conservatively, always five prime to three prime, so one strand is leading and one is made in Okazaki fragments.
Mendel gives three to one, nine three three one, and one one one one in a test cross, and chi square tells you if the data fit.
Beyond Mendel: incomplete dominance, codominance, the ABO alleles, a baby's sex set by the father, and X linked traits in men.
Linkage and crossing over give recombination frequencies, which are map distances.
And mutation and polyploidy create the new variation that evolution needs.
